rationale: A clean factorial cross of the archive's two best-performing legs that is not a duplicate of any prior expression, but it is a mechanical leg-swap with no new economic content, so its main value is diagnostic (is durability leg-specific or additive) rather than genuinely novel.

Beyond being another cosmetic valuation-leg swap, the moderator NEG(xsga/(revt-cogs)) is numerically unstable and sign-flipping whenever gross profit is small or negative — exactly the distressed firms that drive the value-trap effect — so the "isolate the valuation channel" diagnosis is confounded by a badly constructed conditioner.

The switch from an asset-based to a margin-based durability hurdle is an economically meaningful distinction and guards against write-down artifacts, but the absolute 10% margin threshold is not industry-adjusted (unlike the IND_RANK legs elsewhere), so the count risks proxying for industry membership rather than franchise durability.

Replacing the bounded TS_RANK with a signed deviation from the firm's own five-year mean yield is a substantive repair that restores a genuinely two-sided short leg and is well-matched to the stated alpha-vs-slope diagnosis; the residual weakness is that unscaled yield deviations are mechanically larger for high-yield firms, so the leg partly reintroduces the cross-sectional value level it claims to demean away.

A cycle-averaged (Graham-Dodd style) earnings denominator is a genuinely new valuation construction in this archive and economically distinct from the spot yields tested so far, though the claim that coverage "stays high" is optimistic given five required annual lags, and averaged dollar earnings will tilt against fast-growing firms in a way that may masquerade as value.

Acceleration is a temporal dimension the archive has not touched and the expression's direction matches the stated inflection hypothesis, but a second difference of annual ROA is very noisy and closely related to published earnings-acceleration results, so the incremental information over the already-tested TREND moderator may be small.
